purpose: An explicit order-of-magnitude thought experiment, not a forecast of V2D production cost.

assumptions.acceptance_rate_source: Do as I Do, 100DOH qualitative quality screen; not a universal acceptance rate
assumptions.expert_cost_source: CHORD single-task L40S training time; a different implementation and task distribution

expert_amortization_scenarios.definition: accepted_clips_per_shared_expert is a hypothetical reuse factor, not a measured generalization result
expert_amortization_scenarios.unchanged_costs: Every raw clip still needs qualification, reconstruction, retargeting, rollout rendering, and quality control; this scenario analysis reduces only the expert-training term.

measured_reconstruction_scenario.timing_rule: First successful production run per module; downloads, setup, failed attempts, cache hits and host-side final alignment are excluded
measured_reconstruction_scenario.scope: A same-configuration extrapolation through hand-object alignment for already accepted clips. Later reconstruction stages, raw-video screening, retargeting, rollout and quality control are outside this term.

interpretation: Per-clip expert optimization cannot be the only scaling mechanism. Expert cost falls linearly with reuse: roughly four accepted clips per expert already brings this isolated term below one year on 1000 GPUs. The research question is therefore whether reference-conditioned experts and automatic verifiers can share across clips while preserving physical success. Measured reconstruction through hand-object alignment already gives a separate 169.2-day term on 1000 RTX 4090 GPUs for the same hypothetical accepted clips; asset caching, temporal reuse and early screening must be optimized alongside expert sharing.
